beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you cancel our anniversary table? The number's on the fridge. Please make the call for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. I'll tell them something's come up and ask to move it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cancel, not move. Don't leave them expecting another date. Give my name and tonight's time; they don't need the reason.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would speakerphone help? You could tell me if I miss anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No speaker, please. If you need to ask me something, cover the mouthpiece. Stay beside me, though.

records.causality: Owner-targeted repair. B4 offers speakerphone; A5 rejects public listening but asks B to stay close and cover the mouthpiece for questions. The correction serves the precise emotional support request.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last in the race, first in route appreciation. Let's compare what we noticed; start with plants, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a speed contest. I got to the finish first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's one category. Count the plants you identified, not how fast you passed them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I named ten. You called every flower a daisy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I win for consistency. One label throughout; please use the same measure for both of us. How many times did you have to change yours?

records.causality: New candidate. B4 defeats the plant-knowledge contest with ten species versus A's repeated daisy label; A5 makes that exact repetition a consistency contest and demands a comparison.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said these invitations need bleeding, so I've brought a red pen. Eighty envelopes still need lettering; that could be your special part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Bleed means printing past the edge. I'm not writing eighty addresses.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, past the edge. I'll read the addresses; you could do those sweeping letters you used on the sample.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's a font on my computer. I'd print labels if someone peeled them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, the digital lettering. I'll peel every one. Would you take charge of making them look like that sample?

records.causality: New candidate. B4 reveals the lettering is a font and offers printing if someone peels labels; A5 adopts the newly learned language and takes the unwanted peeling work to recruit B.
